# `silk/json/value`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse JSON into a tree of values, read fields from it, and write it back.

## When to use
Use [`Json.parse`](#Json.impl.parse) when the shape of a document is not fixed, or when you need only a few fields
of a larger document. Use [`Json.parseExact`](#Json.impl.parseExact) when decimal precision matters: it retains number
spellings without rounding. Both return the same tree. Read fields with [`Json.field`](#Json.impl.field),
[`Json.fieldAt`](#Json.impl.fieldAt), and the `as...` functions. Use [`Json.deserialize`](#Json.impl.deserialize) or [`Json.decode`](#Json.impl.decode) for typed
values and [`Json.serialize`](#Json.impl.serialize) to write them. Use `silk.json.scanner` to read tokens without a tree.

## Details
Parsing is strict (RFC 8259): no comments, no trailing commas, and no duplicate keys in an
object. Arrays and objects keep source order. String escapes are decoded. `Json.parse` keeps
integers that fit in `i64` or `u64` exact and converts other numbers to the nearest `f64`.
`Json.parseExact` keeps every number as a validated decimal spelling with no precision or
exponent bound. If parsing fails, everything that was built is released.

## Errors
- `JsonError` for invalid JSON, duplicate keys, nesting deeper than `MAX_DEPTH` (64), or trailing
  content. `Json.parse` also rejects numbers outside finite `f64`; `Json.parseExact` does not.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the tree.
- `WriterError` from the write functions if the `Writer` fails.

## Gotchas
A borrowed field or string cannot live longer than the [`Value`](#Value) that owns it. The write
functions do not flush the `Writer`.

## Examples
### Read fields from a document
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.json.scanner { JsonError }
import silk.json.value { Json }
import silk.core.option { Option }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let document = run Json.parse(b"{\"id\":42,\"user\":{\"name\":\"Ada\"}}")
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let id = Json.field(&document, "id") |> Json.asI32 |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  let name = Json.field(&document, "user") |> Json.fieldAt("name") |> Json.asString
    |> Option<string>.unwrapOr("")
  if id != 42 || name != "Ada" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Read a typed value directly
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.json.scanner { JsonError }
import silk.json.value { Json }
import silk.collections.list { List }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let values = run Json.deserialize<List<i64>>(b"[1, 2, 39]")
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if List<i64>.length(&values) != 3 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="JsonNumber"></a>

## `JsonNumber`

```silk
pub union JsonNumber
```

An owned JSON number stored as a machine value or as an exact validated decimal spelling.

### Details

`Json.parse` stores an integer written without a fraction or exponent as `Integer` when it fits
in `i64`, or `Unsigned` when it fits only in `u64`. Other numbers become `Float`, rounded to
nearest `f64` with ties to even. `Json.parseExact` stores all numbers as `Decimal`, retaining
their source spelling without a precision or exponent bound. `Decimal` owns its text.

### Gotchas
`Json.write` rejects a `Float` that is not finite. Manually constructed `Decimal` values must
contain a valid JSON number spelling. Borrow with `JsonNumber.view` instead of copying text.

## `Value`

```silk
pub union Value
```

One JSON value: null, a boolean, a number, a string, an array, or an object.

### Details

A `Value` owns all of its children. Use `match` to get the kind, or the `Json.as...` functions
to read a field of a known kind. Arrays and objects keep source order. `Json.parse` converts
numbers to machine values; `Json.parseExact` keeps exact decimal spellings in the same tree.

### Gotchas

A borrowed field or string cannot live longer than the `Value` that owns it.

<a id="Json.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Value ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `bytes` as one complete JSON document and returns its tree.

#### When to use

Use it when the shape of a document is not fixed, or when you need only a few fields of a
larger document. To read a typed value, use [`Json.deserialize`](#Json.impl.deserialize) or [`Json.decode`](#Json.impl.decode).

#### Details

Parsing is strict (RFC 8259): no comments, no trailing commas, and no duplicate keys in an
object. String escapes are decoded when the document is parsed.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` if `bytes` is not one valid JSON value, if an object has a duplicate key, if the
  nesting is deeper than 64, or if content follows the value. The partial tree is dropped.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the tree.

<a id="Json.impl.parseExact"></a>

### Associated function `parseExact`

```silk
pub effect fn parseExact(bytes: &[u8]) -> Value ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses one complete strict JSON document with every number retained as `JsonNumber.Decimal`.
Numbers keep their validated source spelling without rounding or a fixed exponent bound.
String decoding, duplicate-key checks, and the nesting limit are shared with `Json.parse`.

#### Errors
- `JsonError` for invalid JSON, duplicate decoded keys, excessive nesting, or trailing content.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the allocator cannot supply the owned tree and number text.

<a id="Json.impl.decode"></a>

### Associated function `decode`

```silk
pub fn decode<T: Decode>(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<T, JsonError>
```

Reads `bytes` as one complete JSON document of type `T`. It does not allocate.

#### When to use

Use it for types that implement `Decode`, such as numbers and `bool`. Use [`Json.deserialize`](#Json.impl.deserialize)
for types that need memory, such as `String` and `List<T>`.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` if the JSON is not valid, the value does not have type `T` (`TypeMismatch`), a
  number does not fit (`NumberOutOfRange`), or content follows the value (`TrailingContent`).

<a id="Json.impl.serialize"></a>

### Associated function `serialize`

```silk
pub effect fn serialize<T: Serialize>(value: &T, options: &JsonOptions)
    -> () ! JsonError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes `value` as JSON to the `Writer`, with `options`.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` if the nesting is deeper than the limit in `options`, or a float is not finite.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.

#### Examples

##### Write a struct
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.json.codec { Serialize }
import silk.json.object { JsonObject }
import silk.json.output { JsonOptions }
import silk.json.scanner { JsonError }
import silk.json.value { Json }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }

struct CaptureWriter {
  bytes: [u8; 64],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for CaptureWriter {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, value: &[u8]) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer {
    let mut index: usize = 0
    while index < value.length {
      self.bytes[self.length] = value[index]
      self.length = self.length + 1
      index = index + 1
    }
    return ()
  }

  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer {
    return ()
  }
}

fn holds(writer: &CaptureWriter, expected: &[u8]) -> bool {
  if writer.length != expected.length {
    return false
  }
  let mut index: usize = 0
  while index < expected.length {
    if writer.bytes[index] != expected[index] {
      return false
    }
    index = index + 1
  }
  return true
}

struct Point {
  x: i32,
  y: i32,
}

impl Serialize for Point {
  effect fn serialize(self: &Self, options: &JsonOptions) -> ()
    ! JsonError | WriterError
    ? &mut Writer {
    return run JsonObject.begin(options) |> JsonObject.field("x", &self.x)
      |> JsonObject.field("y", &self.y)
      |> JsonObject.end
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! JsonError | WriterError {
  let mut writer = CaptureWriter { bytes: [0; 64], length: 0 }
  let point = Point { x: 3, y: -4 }
  run Json.serialize(&point, &JsonOptions.compact()) |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut writer)
  if !holds(&writer, b"{\"x\":3,\"y\":-4}") {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Json.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(document: &Value) -> () ! JsonError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes `document` as compact JSON to the `Writer`. It does not flush the `Writer`.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` if the nesting is deeper than 64.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.

#### Gotchas

The text goes to the `Writer` in pieces of up to 4 KiB. After a failure, the `Writer` holds
only the pieces passed to it before the failure.

<a id="Json.impl.equal"></a>

### Associated function `equal`

```silk
pub fn equal(left: &Value, right: &Value) -> bool
```

Compares JSON values without allocating. Numbers compare mathematically, arrays compare in
order, and objects compare by decoded key regardless of insertion order. Object keys must be
unique. A nonfinite machine number compares unequal to every value, including itself.
Finite floats are interpreted using their shortest round-tripping decimal spelling.

<a id="Json.impl.numberIsFinite"></a>

### Associated function `numberIsFinite`

```silk
pub fn numberIsFinite(value: &JsonNumber) -> bool
```

Returns false only for a machine float that is NaN or an infinity.
Exact decimal spellings are finite mathematical numbers even when their exponents are huge.

<a id="Json.impl.compareNumbers"></a>

### Associated function `compareNumbers`

```silk
pub fn compareNumbers(left: &JsonNumber, right: &JsonNumber) -> i32
```

Returns -1, 0, or 1 according to the mathematical order of two finite JSON numbers.
Decimal and integer variants remain exact. Floats use their shortest round-tripping decimal
spelling. No heap storage is needed. Both numbers must be finite; otherwise this traps.

<a id="Json.impl.isIntegerNumber"></a>

### Associated function `isIntegerNumber`

```silk
pub fn isIntegerNumber(value: &JsonNumber) -> bool
```

Returns whether a finite JSON number is mathematically integral without allocating.
Decimal and integer variants remain exact; floats use their shortest round-tripping decimal
spelling. The number must be finite; otherwise this traps.

<a id="Json.impl.multipleOfNumbers"></a>

### Associated function `multipleOfNumbers`

```silk
pub effect fn multipleOfNumbers(value: &JsonNumber, divisor: &JsonNumber) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns whether a finite JSON number is an exact integer multiple of a positive divisor.
Returns false for nonpositive divisors. Decimal and integer variants remain exact; floats
use their shortest round-tripping decimal spelling. Both numbers must be finite.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if decimal arithmetic scratch storage cannot be allocated.

#### Gotchas
Traps for a NaN or infinite machine-number argument.

<a id="Json.impl.asUsizeNumber"></a>

Converts a finite JSON number to `usize` if nonnegative, integral, and in range.
Returns `None` for fractions, negatives, or overflow. Negative zero becomes zero.
Floats use their shortest round-tripping decimal spelling. No allocation is needed.
The number must be finite; otherwise this traps.

<a id="JsonDocument"></a>

## `JsonDocument`

```silk
pub struct JsonDocument
```

A parsed JSON document kept in two flat buffers: one record for each value, in source order,
and the decoded text of every string and key.

### When to use

Use it to read a document. Parsing allocates about two buffers in all, instead of one for each
string, array, and object as [`Json.parse`](#Json.impl.parse) does, and dropping it frees only those buffers. Use
a [`Value`](#Value) tree when you need to build or change a document; [`JsonDocument.toValue`](#JsonDocument.impl.toValue) makes one.

### Details

A value is named by a [`JsonNode`](#JsonNode), a position in its document. An array record is followed by
its elements, and an object record by each key and its value, so a node's children are the
records after it. Each array and object knows where its last child ends, so skipping a value is
one step.

### Gotchas

A `JsonNode` is only meaningful with the document that returned it. With another document it
names some other value or traps.

### Examples
#### Read fields of a parsed document
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.json.scanner { JsonError }
import silk.json.value { JsonDocument, JsonNode }

effect fn read() -> i32 ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let document = run JsonDocument.parse(b"{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"tags\":[1,2,3]}")
  let root = JsonDocument.root(&document)
  let tags = match JsonDocument.field(&document, root, "tags") {
    Option<JsonNode>.Some { value } => value
    Option<JsonNode>.None => { return 1 }
  }
  if JsonDocument.length(&document, tags) != 3 {
    return 2
  }
  let name = match JsonDocument.field(&document, root, "name") {
    Option<JsonNode>.Some { value } => value
    Option<JsonNode>.None => { return 3 }
  }
  return match JsonDocument.asString(&document, name) {
    Option<string>.Some { value } => if value == "Ada" { 0 } else { 4 }
    Option<string>.None => 4
  }
}

effect fn program() -> i32 ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run read() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}

effect fn failed(error: JsonError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 5
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), failed)
}
```

```silk
pub struct JsonMember
```

One member of an object in a [`JsonDocument`](#JsonDocument): the node of its key, which is a string, and the
node of its value.



<a id="JsonDocument.impl"></a>

```silk
impl JsonDocument
```

<a id="JsonDocument.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> JsonDocument ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `bytes` as one complete JSON document.

#### Details

Parsing is strict (RFC 8259), with the same rules and errors as [`Json.parse`](#Json.impl.parse): no comments,
no trailing commas, no duplicate keys, nesting at most 64 deep, and nothing after the value.
String escapes are decoded when the document is parsed, and numbers are converted to a
[`JsonNumber`](#JsonNumber).

#### Errors

- `JsonError` if `bytes` is not one valid JSON value, with the reason and offset that
  [`Json.parse`](#Json.impl.parse) reports.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the buffers.

<a id="JsonDocument.impl.asNumber"></a>

### Method `asNumber`

```silk
pub fn asNumber<'a>(self: &'a Self, node: JsonNode) -> Option<JsonNumberView<'a>>
```

Returns a borrowed view of a number, or `None` if `node` is not a number.
This operation does not allocate. Decimal text borrows the document and cannot outlive it.

<a id="JsonDocument.impl.asString"></a>

### Method `asString`

```silk
pub fn asString<'a>(self: &'a Self, node: JsonNode) -> Option<string<'a>>
```

Returns the text of a string, with escapes decoded. Returns an absent option if `node` is not
a string. The text is borrowed from the document.

<a id="JsonDocument.impl.toValue"></a>

### Method `toValue`


<a id="JsonDocument.impl.write"></a>

### Method `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(self: &Self) -> () ! JsonError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes the document as compact JSON to the `Writer`. It does not flush the `Writer`.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` with reason `InvalidNumber` for a float that is not finite, which only
  [`JsonDocument.fromValue`](#JsonDocument.impl.fromValue) can store.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.

#### Gotchas

The text goes to the `Writer` in pieces of up to 4 KiB. After a failure, the `Writer` holds
only the pieces passed to it before the failure.

<a id="JsonDocument.impl.writeWith"></a>

### Method `writeWith`

```silk
pub effect fn writeWith(self: &Self, options: &JsonOptions) -> () ! JsonError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes the document as JSON to the `Writer`, with the indentation and depth limit of
`options`. It does not flush the `Writer`.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` if the nesting is deeper than the limit in `options`, or with reason
  `InvalidNumber` for a float that is not finite.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.
